fields.aka: Murāri, Rasika Murāri, Rasikānanda Deva Gosvāmī
fields.appearance: Kārtika Śukla Pratipat (Dīpāvalī night), 1512 Śaka (1590 CE), at Rohiṇī (Rayaṇī) on the Subarṇarekhā
fields.disappearance: Phālguna Śukla Pratipat, 1574 Śaka (1652 CE), at Remuṇā (entered Kṣīra-corā Gopīnātha)
fields.place: Rohiṇī (Rayaṇī), Mallabhūmi; Gopīvallabhapura (Rādhā-Govinda); Remuṇā (samādhi); Kuñja Maṭha, Purī (Rādhā-Rasika Rāya)
fields.works: Śyāmānanda-śataka; Śrīmad-bhāgavatāṣṭaka; Kuñja-keli-dvādaśaka; hymns and songs
fields.notes: Foremost disciple of Śyāmānanda Prabhu. Son of Rājā Acyutadeva (Acyutānanda) of Rohiṇī and Bhavānī Devī; wife Śyāmadāsī of Ghāṭaśilā; sons Rādhānanda, Kṛṣṇagovinda and Rādhākṛṣṇa, ancestors of the Mahāntas of Gopīvallabhapura. Given the service of Rādhā-Govinda at Gopīvallabhapura. Converted kings (Vaidyanātha Bhañja of Mayurbhañj, Gajapati of Pāṭaspur, Candrabhānu of Moyna), Muslims, robbers, a wild elephant (Gopāla dāsa) and two tigers (Bhakti-ratnākara 15.81-86). Jagannātha's chariot waited for him. His life: Rasika-maṅgala by Gopījana-vallabha dāsa.

fields.name: Hṛdaya Caitanya
fields.notes: Dearest disciple of Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita, who named him Hṛdaya Caitanya after Gaura-Nityānanda danced in his kīrtana by the Ganges, and gave him the service of the Deities at Ambikā-Kālnā. Son of Vāṇīnātha, nephew of Gadādhara (Śākhā-nirṇayāmṛta 58). Dīkṣā guru of Śyāmānanda (whom he named Kṛṣṇadāsa); Rādhā rebuked him in a dream for scolding Śyāmānanda over his new tilaka. His son married Gaurīdāsa's granddaughter; the gosvāmīs of Ambikā descend from him.

Vārendra brāhmaṇa scholar of Gambhilā (Gāmlā, Murshidabad) who fed and taught five hundred students; disciple of Narottama Ṭhākura despite being a brāhmaṇa (Prema-vilāsa 20; Narottama-vilāsa 10). Brought to Narottama through Harirāma Ācārya. With Rāmacandra Kavirāja defeated the smārtas at Kumārapura. Wife Nārāyaṇī Devī, daughter Viṣṇupriyā; adopted son Kṛṣṇacaraṇa (son of Rāmakṛṣṇa Ācārya). Viśvanātha Cakravartī was his student.

fields.place: Goyās (confluence of the Ganges and the Padmā)
fields.notes: Brāhmaṇa disciple of Narottama Ṭhākura. Son of the Śākta Śivānanda (Śivāi) Ācārya of Goyās; elder brother Harirāma Ācārya (disciple of Rāmacandra Kavirāja). The brothers let go the goats for Durgā-pūjā after meeting Narottama, and defeated the paṇḍita Murāri of Mithilā (Narottama-vilāsa 10). Wife Kanakalatikā Devī; sons Rādhākṛṣṇa (died young) and Kṛṣṇacaraṇa, adopted by Gaṅgānārāyaṇa Cakravartī, teacher of Viśvanātha Cakravartī. Descendants at Saidābād; the king of Manipur is their disciple (Prema-vilāsa 20; Bhakti-ratnākara 15.121-122).

fields.name: Santoṣa Datta
fields.aka: Santosa Datta (Rāya), Santoṣa Rāya, Vasanta Datta
fields.place: Kheturī; founded Vasantapura at Śiyālā near Kheturī
fields.notes: Son of Puruṣottama Datta, the elder paternal uncle (others: younger) of Narottama Ṭhākura, and his disciple. A learned minister of the king of Gauḍa, expert in government; became king of Kheturī after Kṛṣṇānanda and Puruṣottama died (Bhakti-ratnākara 1.468-469; Narottama-vilāsa 2). Celebrated in his kingdom the recovery of the Gosvāmīs' books (Bhakti-ratnākara 7.269); built the temple and bore the whole cost of the Kheturī festival and the installation of the six Deities; welcomed Śyāmānanda (7.308). The Saṅgīta-mādhava of Govinda Kavirāja was written at his request. Some say his other name was Vasanta Datta.
